sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Fataleka language [far] (Internet Archive copy of Dec 2024).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog only. Lists no language description for Fataleka: Capell PARADISEC recordings (AC1-415, AC1-433) and a Swadesh list (AC2-SINMALA102), Simons 1980 (Malaitan pronoun systems), a 1980 West Fataleka book of Jonah, Ethnologue and Glottolog entries.

sources.citation: Farongoe Lea Ana Fataleka: Fataleka New Testament. SITAG / Wycliffe Bible Translators, 2017 (eBible.org id far / FARWBT).
sources.note: Scripture text in a practical orthography (details page read online); no linguistic front matter; confirms SITAG translation work exists but no accompanying phonology statement was found.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1986. Wai: a Malaitan language in Fiji. In P. Geraghty, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), FOCAL II: Papers from the Fourth International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, 435-463. Pacific Linguistics C-94. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 'Wai phonology' (pp.447-448, Table 3-1) gives only the segment inventory and phonemic vowel length; no statement on stress or accent anywhere in the paper. Describes Wai, a Fiji immigrant variety derived from mixed North Malaitan dialects (Lau, To'abaita, Baelelea, Baegu, Fataleka), not Fataleka as spoken on Malaita.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B.D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Fataleka is wordlist no. 68; comparative wordlists and reflex/sound-correspondence tables only. a full-text search for stress/accent/penultimate finds nothing relevant; no prosodic statement for any language.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. Field recordings and notes, North Malaita: PARADISEC AC1-433 'Malaita Island (north and south), Guadalcanal Island' (1970) and AC2-SINMALA102 Swadesh list.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only archival primary material tagged for Fataleka; Capell's notes sometimes carry accent marks or a prosodic remark. PARADISEC catalog was bot-could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Ivens, Walter G. 1930. The Island Builders of the Pacific. London: Seeley, Service & Co. (archive.org item islandbuildersof0000walt, scanned text).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp.27-28 group the North Mala languages ('Tali Kali, Fata Leka, Kwara 'Ae are closer akin to one another..') with a few consonant remarks (prenasalisation, glottal 'break'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lichtenberk, Frantisek. 2008. A Grammar of Toqabaqita. (Mouton Grammar Library 42.) Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. Ch. 2 (phonology, incl. stress).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6254.M271 L53 2008); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright); also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6254.M271 L53 2008
sources.note: Closest fully described North Malaitan lect (toab1237); Ross 1973 (quoted in Siegel 1986:446) holds that 'all North Malaitan dialects share essentially the same grammar'. Would supply the family-internal expectation for Fataleka stress, but only as a proxy under a different glottocode, not a Fataleka statement.

sources.citation: Guidieri, Remo. 1980. La route des morts: introduction à la vie cérémonielle Fataleka. Paris: Seuil. (and Guidieri 1972 JSO 28(37):323-335, full PDF).

sources.note: Long-term fieldworker among the Fataleka; the monograph may contain a note on transcription/pronunciation of Fataleka terms. Low probability of a stress statement.

sources.citation: SITAG / Wycliffe (Solomon Islands Translation Advisory Group). Unpublished Fataleka orthography statement / phonology write-up prepared for the Fataleka New Testament (Farongoe Lea Ana Fataleka, 2017).

sources.note: A completed NT translation by SITAG normally rests on an orthography/phonology statement; this is the only plausible first-hand modern description of Fataleka sound structure, and such statements usually include a line on stress.
